commit.message:
[new release] colibri2 (4 packages) (0.7)

CHANGES:

### Highlights
  - DSeq, a theory of sequences with a default value, is now the common
    backend of the arrays, the n-sequences and the sequences (Hichem Rami
    Ait-El-Hara, OCamlPro): shared slices, difference witnesses, decisions
    on equality, models; arrays with constant arrays, `nseq.content`,
    conversions between integers and bit sequences, reversal.
  - Many domains are written in WhyML and proved with Why3, then extracted
    to OCaml (library colibrilib, `common/colibrilib/`): the domain of the
    reals (union of intervals and congruence), the bit-vector domain (BDD),
    known bits, the floating-point domain on concrete binary floats (with
    the rounding of Flocq), the dyadic domain, the numbers (Zarith, Flint),
    the ring normal form and the rewriting of `mod`, the acyclicity of the
    datatypes.
  - The bit-vector domain is the BDD: it solves the non-linear identities
    and was faster on all the bit-vector benchmarks. Integer bitwise
    operators are reasoned on in the same domain, for any integer.
  - Floating-point rules ported from COLIBRI (relations from the
    comparisons, monotonicity, symbolic rules), and direct backward
    propagation of the multiplication, division and conversions.
  - The model check evaluates the bit-vector operators with code proved
    equal to the definitions of SMT-LIB 2.7.
  - Quantifiers: the attribute `:rewrite-rule` on an assertion
    `(forall (...) (! (= lhs rhs) :rewrite-rule))` makes it an oriented
    rewrite rule: each match of `lhs` is replaced by `rhs`, and the matched
    term is no longer used for matching. With the experimental option
    `--quantifier-add-safe-axiom-as-rewrite-rules`, the axioms that look
    like rewrite rules are used as such without the attribute.
  - Fixes of the matching: the multi-patterns were not used; matching
    waits for the congruence closure and for the disequalities before
    instantiating; one trie per quantifier avoids duplicate
    instantiations; the substitution simplifies the Boolean connectives
    and lets the theories close by congruence; the triggers keep the
    variables bound before a skipped builtin; the atoms
    `colibri_array_submem` are not triggers.
  - The datatypes are checked acyclic (incremental negative cycle
    detection).
  - Differential fuzzers (`make fuzz`) for integers, bit-vectors,
    datatypes and floating-points.

### Breaking changes
  - Arrays, n-sequences and sequences use DSeq by default; the previous
    procedures with `--array-nseq`, `--array-nseqs-no-ppg`, `--nseq-shs`,
    `--nseq-base`, `--nseq-ext`.
  - Removed: the linear boolean ring for bit-vectors and `--bv-use-bdd`,
    `--sort-last-effort`, the executable `colibri2_stage0`.
  - The factorization of `Dom_product` with new terms needs
    `--lra-factorize`; the ring normal form is on by default
    (`--lra-no-ring`, `--lra-ring-max-terms`, `--lra-no-mod-rewrite`).
  - Ground assertions are delayed, the last ones first
    (`--no-delay-ground-assertions`, `--shift-assertions-priority`).
  - `float-threshold-max-repeat` is 100 (was 5000).
  - Exit code 125 when Flint cannot decide a comparison or the rationality
    of an algebraic number.
  - The extracted OCaml modules are `colibrilib__<file>__<Module>`.
  - Dependencies: dolmen 0.11 (SMT-LIB 2.7), flint >= 0.5.0, camlid >= 0.3.

### New builtins
  - `(DSeq T)`: `dseq.length`, `dseq.default`, `dseq.get`, `dseq.const`,
    `dseq.set`, `dseq.extract`, `dseq.update`, `dseq.diff`, `dseq.rev`,
    `dseq.from_array`, `dseq.update_seq_with_array`, `dseq.int_to_seq`,
    `dseq.seq_to_int`; on arrays: `colibri_array_update`,
    `colibri_array_update_with_seq`, `colibri_array_submem`.
  - Integer bitwise operators: `colibri_and_int`, `colibri_ior_int`,
    `colibri_xor_int`, `colibri_not_int`, `colibri_rshift_int`,
    `colibri_testbit_int`, `colibri_extract_int`,
    `colibri_signed_extract_int`, `colibri_update_int`.
  - Attribute `:rewrite-rule` on quantified equations (see the highlights).

### Fixes of wrong answers
  - `(bvsdiv s 0)` is 2^n-1 when s >= 0; `(bvsmod s 0) = s` is checked.
  - `fp.to_real` linearization with a non-finite argument; `of_ieee_bits`
    on NaN ranges; backward `fp.add` on overflow.
  - Rationality and hash of the algebraic numbers (Flint 0.5.0).
  - Model check of non-integer values given to Int arguments.

### Other changes
  - The sign and abs solvers of the products are complete when one side
    is non-zero.
  - The default theories are the library `colibri2.theories.default`
    (`Colibri2_default_theories.theories`), for the users of colibri2 as a
    library.
